jobs.description:
*Over een paar jaar draait ons platform in gebouwen door heel Europa. Hoe de back\-end daaronder in elkaar zit, bepaal jij.*

*Je komt als senior binnen bij de marktleider in AI\-SaaS voor commercieel vastgoed, precies nu we uitrollen naar België, Luxemburg en Duitsland. Jouw architectuurkeuzes verdwijnen niet in een comité: ze worden de basis waar het hele team op bouwt.*

**Over Healthy Workers**


Healthy Workers is AI\-SaaS\-marktleider binnen gebouwoptimalisatie voor commercieel vastgoed. Eigenaren van commercieel vastgoed staan onder flinke druk om hun gebouwen te verduurzamen. Ons platform helpt ze daarbij: we verbinden de installaties en data van een gebouw en laten het slimmer draaien, met minder energieverbruik en meer comfort tot gevolg. We zitten direct aan tafel met die eigenaren. Na Nederland rollen we nu uit in België, Luxemburg en Duitsland, en daarna volgt de rest van Europa.


We zijn een scale\-up: informeel, korte lijnen, en direct contact met onze founders Jonatan en Guus.

**Wat ga je doen?**


Je komt in team Product als senior back\-end developer. Je bouwt zelf mee, en je zorgt dat het team en het platform de volgende groeistap aankunnen als het gaat om de back\-end.


* Je bepaalt de architectuur van de back\-end en legt besluiten vast, zodat niemand over een jaar hoeft te raden waarom iets zo gebouwd is
* Je maakt het platform klaar voor Europa: schaalbaar, snel en betrouwbaar, van API tot infrastructuur
* Je bouwt mee aan AI\-features die gebouwinstallaties slimmer aansturen
* Samen met ons Data\-team en SkySpark (ons platform voor gebouwanalyse) maak je Healthy Workers dé plek voor alle gebouw\- en klantdata
* Je houdt de productie gezond en de bug\-backlog onder controle
* Je coacht collega's, reviewt code binnen één werkdag en zorgt dat geen enkele service aan één persoon hangt


Zo ziet je week er ongeveer uit:


\~60% bouwen: API's, datamodellen, integraties en AI\-features


\~20% maintenance, devops en infra: bugs, monitoring, CI/CD en schaalbaarheid


\~10% code reviews en security (pentests en ISO)


\~10% stand\-ups, refinement, sprintplanning en retro

**Onze stack**


Kotlin, Micronaut, MySQL, BigQuery, Docker, Kubernetes, GitLab CI, Terraform, Google Cloud Platform en SkySpark. We plannen in Linear.

**Kom je uit Java?** Perfect! Kotlin voelt al snel vertrouwd, en met jouw JVM\-ervaring zit je er binnen een paar weken in.

**Wat neem je mee?**


Must\-haves:

* Ruime ervaring als back\-end developer met Java of Kotlin
* Je hebt API's en datamodellen ontworpen voor systemen die groeien, en je hebt architectuurkeuzes gemaakt waar je daarna zelf mee verder moest
* Je bent gewend eigenaar te zijn van productie: debuggen, monitoren en incidenten oplossen
* Je werkt vanzelfsprekend met Docker, Kubernetes en CI/CD
* Je maakt anderen beter met constructieve reviews, kennis delen en goede documentatie
* Je spreekt vloeiend Engels en woont in Nederland

**Mooi meegenomen:**

* Ervaring met Terraform, GitLab CI of Google Cloud Platform
* Kennis van C\#
* Ervaring met security en certificering, zoals ISO
* Affiniteit met gebouw\-, energie\- of sensordata

**Wat krijg je terug?**

* Een salaris dat past bij je ervaring. Dat bespreken we open in het eerste gesprek
* Een SAR\-regeling, zodat je meedeelt in de groei van Healthy Workers
* 30 vakantiedagen
* Een opleidings\- en conferentiebudget
* Reiskostenvergoeding voor woon\-werkverkeer
* Geen piketdienst
* Echt mandaat: je spart direct met onze Founders Jonatan en Guus over waar de back\-end naartoe gaat

**Het proces**


Van eerste gesprek tot beslissing duurt het maximaal 2 weken. Na elk gesprek hoor je de volgende dag van ons, zonder weken stilte.

**Klinkt dit als jouw volgende stap?**


Solliciteer via onderstaande button of stuur me een berichtje. Je cv of gewoon je LinkedIn\-profiel is genoeg, een motivatiebrief is niet nodig. Wil je eerst sparren of dit iets voor je is? Neem gerust contact op, dan hebben we het erover: Maarten Wolters maarten@healthyworkers.com of \+31 6 13392042\.

It all started when engineer Fred Luddy wrote code that automated a tedious task for his coworker, Phyllis. She cried tears of joy. Join us to put AI to work for people.

 **Job Description**  

The ServiceNow Partner Design Studio is looking for a Partner Solution Engineer with a passion for innovation, design standards, and cutting\-edge architecture practices. This is a unique opportunity to shape partner\-branded solutions using an AI\-first approach — where AI is embedded into every step of design and solutioning. As a pooled, forward\-deployed engineering authority, you will work across partners as a force multiplier focused on standards, reuse, and quality, certifying into Practices to bring domain depth where it’s needed. As a Partner Solution Engineer, you will define the reference architectures, design standards, and validated patterns that partners build to — serving as the forward\-deployed technical authority for AI\-infused ServiceNow solutions that address real\-world business challenges.

jobs.description:
**Looking to race into your next role? Strap in, we're looking for a Multiphysics Simulation Engineer to join our unique mission!**

***About Formula E:***


Formula E, the world's fastest\-growing sport, is redefining motorsport with a bold focus on innovation and sustainability.


Hosting over 150 races in iconic cities globally and backed by top manufacturers like Porsche, Nissan and Jaguar, we feature elite drivers and cutting\-edge EV technology.
  

  

As the world's first certified B Corp sport and the first sport certified to the British Standards Institution (BSI) Net Zero Pathway. Formula E combines thrilling entertainment with a mission to advance sustainable progress, inspiring a global fanbase with our high\-performance brand new GEN4 car capable of hitting speeds of 335kph and reaching 200kph in just 4\.4 seconds. Currently achieving 0\-100 kmh in 1\.8 seconds.


Using the spectacle of sport, we are sending a powerful and meaningful message to help alter perceptions and speed\-up the switch to electric mobility.

***The Role:***


As our Multiphysics Simulation Engineer, you will turn complex physical problems into clear, practical recommendations to support the development of next\-generation all\-electric race cars and trackside technical systems.


Using COMSOL Multiphysics as your principal simulation platform, you will solve coupled electrical, electromagnetic, thermal, fluid, and structural challenges. Beyond component\-level modelling, you will connect subsystem models into comprehensive virtual representations of the car, laying the groundwork for Formula E’s future digital\-twin capabilities. You will collaborate closely with internal technical teams, the FIA, automotive manufacturers, technical partners, and test teams.

**Key Responsibilities**

* **Multiphysics Modeling:** Develop, run, and interpret 3D simulation models in COMSOL Multiphysics across electrical, electromagnetic, thermal, CFD, and structural domains.
* **High\-Voltage \& Powertrain Analysis:** Model and investigate electric machines, battery packs, power electronics, EV charging systems, high\-voltage cabling, busbars, connectors, and sensors.
* **Thermal \& Fluid Dynamics:** Perform thermal and CFD analyses of cooling systems, internal/external airflow, pressure losses, and conjugate heat transfer.
* **Structural Mechanics:** Conduct structural analyses covering stress, deformation, stiffness, vibration, fatigue, and thermal loading.
* **Geometry \& Meshing:** Prepare and simplify CAD geometry and build computational meshes tailored for accurate numerical solving.
* **Test Data Correlation \& Optimisation:** Correlate virtual models with lab, rig, supplier, and track\-test data, running parametric and optimization studies to enhance performance, efficiency, safety, and reliability.
* **System Integration \& Digital Twins:** Connect component models into larger virtual representations of the race car, helping establish validation and configuration practices for digital\-twin development.
* **Technical Communication:** Clearly communicate simulation assumptions, solver settings, limitations, and actionable findings during technical reviews.

* Educational Background: An MEng or MSc in electrical, electronic, mechanical, automotive, aerospace, computational, or mechatronics engineering, applied physics, or a closely related discipline. (Electrical/electronic engineering combined with 3D CAE experience is highly preferred).

* Technical Domain Expertise: Practical experience in 3D physics\-based modeling across electrical/electromagnetics, thermal management, CFD, or structural mechanics. Experience with EV high\-voltage systems or electric powertrains is a strong advantage.
* Tooling \& Numerical Methods: Solid understanding of numerical methods, boundary conditions, mesh quality, and solver convergence. COMSOL Multiphysics experience is advantageous, though experience with other major professional CAE tools is welcome.
* CAD \& Data Correlation: Experience preparing CAD geometry and correlating simulation models with physical test/telemetry data.
* Mindset \& Approach: Strong engineering judgment with the ability to translate numerical outputs into concrete design recommendations. Excellent written and verbal communication skills to present methods and findings clearly to technical stakeholders.

***What's in it for you?***

* Opportunity to extend your stay if travelling for a race event

* Enhanced Parental Leave

* Cycle to Work and Electric Car Scheme

*This is a hybrid role and you'll be required to do 3 days a week in our Hammersmith London office*

***Application Process***


Think you’ve got what it takes to join our race to the future?


The closing date for this role is **14th October 2026**, however if we receive a high volume of applications we may close it early.


At Formula E, we are building a culture where every voice matters, every perspective accelerates progress, and every individual is empowered to rise, contribute boldly, and shape a better world \- together. We will provide equal opportunities regardless of an individuals' protected characteristics. We believe in attracting and retaining diverse talent to strengthen our global vision with a variety of experiences, backgrounds and perspectives.

**Our mission is clear. The message is simple. Whoever you are. However you live. Whatever you believe. Formula E. For the Future. For Everyone.**

**We’ll see you at the starting line!**

We are the UK's biggest port, central to the country's economy and ambitions for growth. We connect the UK to the world, but we are much more than a conventional port.

Write clear, testable Python code and contribute to documentation, code reviews, version control and automated testing and deployment.
Monitor applications and workflows, investigate technical issues and work with colleagues to resolve them.
Gather feedback from scientific users and translate it into practical improvements to the tools you help build.
Explore relevant AI technologies, including generative AI and AI agents, with guidance from experienced colleagues.
Share what you learn and contribute to technical discussions within the team.

An interest in applying engineering skills to scientific research.
Fluent English, both written and spoken.

Cloud platforms such as AWS, container tools such as Docker, and CI/CD workflows.
APIs, databases and data processing pipelines.
Deploying, monitoring or maintaining machine learning applications.
Building generative AI applications or working with AI agents.
Some grounding in life sciences or scientific research, gained through your studies, projects or work experience. Specialist knowledge of biology or antibody discovery is not required.

EUR59.568,00---89.352,00

Benefits

When you join Genmab, you become a part of a culture that supports your physical, financial, social, and emotional well-being. Our benefits include, but are not limited to:

Pension

Employee support programs

Build the tool our engineers use to run a quantum computing platform

Horizon Quantum's platform compiles and executes quantum programs on real quantum processors around the world. Every day, jobs flow through it: submitted, compiled, queued, run, returned. When one of those jobs fails, our engineers currently piece the story together from several systems at once.

You'll build the tool that fixes that. Over the course of the internship, a small team of interns will design and ship an internal operations platform that gives our Engineering and Support teams a single place to monitor the system, investigate failures, and act on live jobs. It will be used by the people sitting next to you, and it may still be in use after you go back to college.

About Horizon Quantum And Triple Alpha

Horizon Quantum is building software infrastructure that empowers developers to use quantum computing to solve the world’s toughest computational problems. Founded in 2018 by Dr. Joe Fitzsimons, a leading researcher, UCD alumnus and former professor with more than two decades of experience in quantum computing, the company is bridging the gap between today’s quantum hardware and tomorrow’s applications through the creation of advanced software development tools. Its integrated development environment, Triple Alpha, enables developers to write sophisticated, hardware-agnostic quantum programs at multiple levels of abstraction.

Built with proprietary Turing-complete languages and an optimizing compiler, Triple Alpha empowers developers to build complex hardware-agnostic quantum programs. In Triple Alpha, users can work at multiple levels of abstraction—from higher-level algorithm design to hardware-specific control.

Beyond higher-level programming tools, Triple Alpha gives developers access to advanced capabilities supported by Horizon’s underlying execution infrastructure. Users can code, compile, and optimize programs seamlessly across a range of processors and simulators, with built-in resource analysis and single-step API deployment.

What you'll build

A web application, backed by real services and real data, with the following at its core:

A searchable, filterable view of every job the platform has processed and the ability to drill into any one of them for the full picture.
Operational control and job management.
Integration between jobs and engineering tickets.
Live visibility into platform health and usage through dashboards and alerts.

How the internship runs

You'll work as a team, with our teams, and with a real degree of design authority and mentorship from our full time engineers throughout.

Requirements and investigation. Understand the existing system and its data model. Decide what's in scope and what isn't. Identify the constraints you're working within.
System design. Produce the architecture, including components and services, data flows, API specification, data access design, security and authorisation model, error handling, logging and monitoring, deployment, testing strategy. You'll present and defend this before writing production standard code.
Implementation. Build it, using the practices we use: Git, code review, issue tracking, automated testing, coding standards, separated environments, secure credential handling.
Testing. Unit, API, integration, frontend and end-to-end tests, covering the failure paths as seriously as the happy ones.
Documentation and handover. Architecture, local setup, deployment, configuration, API reference, troubleshooting, known limitations, and where you'd take it next.

You'll present your progress and findings to the wider Horizon Quantum team as you go.

What you'll come away with

A production system in use by professional engineers, and the story of how you designed it.
Full-stack experience, including frontend, services, APIs, data, integrations, observability, and deployment.
Practice at the parts of engineering that courses rarely teach, such as scoping ambiguous requirements, defending an architecture, writing documentation someone else needs, and building something secure enough to point at production.
A working understanding of how a commercial quantum computing platform actually operates.
Colleagues and a network in one of the most interesting corners of today’s technology industry.

You don't need a quantum computing background. You need to be a capable software engineer who wants to be challenged.
